payload.feature:
LANDING PR for story #415 (dead hands servers leak their scratch trees into the RAM-backed /tmp).

Branch story-415-hands-scratch-reap has five signed commits on main 5921f900:
- c6412f0f, from implement-story-415-dead-hands-s-ebb878bb, held for security. A hands session's tree is locked for its owner's life, removed on SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP, and reaped at the next start once its owner is dead.
- 30361c99, from remediate-story-415-a-dead-hands-ab4c3ddf, held for security. A session that cannot lock refuses. The reaper keeps and says a tree whose lock it cannot probe, opens the lock without blocking or following links, and reads a Linux zombie as dead. The reap moved to the CLI's drive_to_end: one stderr line per tree, nothing journaled.
- 60859561 and 221b1c48, from remediate-story-415-again-a-dead-2534918e, ruled residual/low and shipped. A tree appears only locked: it is built under .staging-<name>, then renamed. The lockless transition is named and pinned. The macOS mknodat build break is fixed with mkfifo. hands serve's stderr refusal line is pinned.
- 6bb4f43e, the controller's commit. The reaped line's fixed text becomes one constant so its write fits one covered line (the exact gate was one line short), with identical bytes.

OPERATOR RULING (2026-09-28), binding on this run: a ONE-RELEASE TRANSITION for lockless trees. A tree with no .owner.lock (from a server before #415) whose recorded pid reads dead here is still reaped through 0.12.0. 0.13.0 ends that, and TODO(0.13.0 marks the line. The operator accepts that during the transition a live pre-#415 server in a foreign pid namespace sharing TMPDIR can have its tree reaped. That is not a finding here.

The public-API ratchet grows brokkr-protocol from 303 to 320 items: Session, SessionError, Reaped and reap_dead_sessions replace session_dir. signal-hook 0.3.18 becomes a direct dependency of brokkr-protocol; it was already in the lockfile. Decision 0071 gains a PROPOSED addendum.

Judge:
1. Whether a live owner's tree can be removed outside the ruled transition. Consider a locked tree, a tree mid-creation, a tree whose lock cannot be probed, a zombie owner, and a symlink or FIFO planted as the lock. Also consider whether a reap can hang an engine start.
2. Whether hands serve fails closed when its lock cannot be taken, names the path and errno, and leaves no half-made tree.
3. Whether the module doc, probe()'s comment and the 0071 addendum say exactly what the code does, including the transition and its end, and whether the addendum is marked proposed.
4. Whether anything is Linux-only that must also build or run on macOS (decision 0063).

Threat model (operator ruling, 2026-09-26): catch realistic accidental misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read. The transition above is the one ruled exception.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051 so the contribution gate can vouch for it. If a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding, prove it with a test bound by a compiling mutation, commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",

members.adversarial:
Adversarial review of the #415 landing branch, base 5921f900, HEAD 6bb4f43e (five commits). I tried to break the reap and the session lock; no fail-open and no live owner's tree removed outside the ruled transition, so nothing high/security. Two low residuals remain.

LOW 1 - untrusted filesystem names are printed raw to the terminal. crates/brokkr-cli/src/lib.rs:508 does `eprint!("{}", reap_dead_sessions())`, and Reaped's Display (session.rs:162-174) interpolates `tree.display()` with no Safe/safe_lines pass. owner_pid() accepts any label between `brokkr-hands-` and `-<pid>-<uuid>`, so a local process with write access to TMPDIR can plant a directory whose name carries ESC/newline/bidi bytes and a dead pid, with no .owner.lock. Concrete, reproduced input: a directory named `brokkr-hands-serve\x1b[2Jforged\nline-<dead-pid>-<uuid>` under TMPDIR. The next run/resume/rerun prints `hands: reaped <path>...` with the raw 0x1b and a forged second line on stderr (my scratch binary against the built brokkr-protocol emitted `"hands: reaped /tmp/.../brokkr-hands-serve\u{1b}[2Jforged\nline-<pid>-<uuid>: ..."`). The house already routes operator-facing text through render::Safe (its doc and render/tests.rs::control_characters_never_reach_the_terminal assert `!contains('\x1b')`, and report_to uses safe_lines on stderr), so this is a real output-integrity regression, though it only manipulates what the operator sees. Fix: pass the Reaped text through Safe/safe_lines in drive_to_end (or sanitize in the Display).

LOW 2 - the create-lock-file failure path leaks a permanent staging tree. session.rs:105-108: `create_dir_all(&staged)?` then the Session struct literal runs `File::create(staged.join(LOCK))?`; if File::create fails (EMFILE/ENFILE, EDQUOT, ENOSPC, EISDIR on a planted .owner.lock) the `?` returns before any Session exists, so no Drop removes the `.staging-` directory. Concrete input: fd exhaustion or a full RAM-backed /tmp while TMPDIR is writable. The leaked name is exactly the one owner_pid() rejects, so the reaper never collects it - a leak of the very kind #415 exists to close (bounded: one empty dir per failed refusal). The later flock-refusal path does drop the staged tree (test a_session_that_cannot_lock_refuses_and_leaves_no_tree), so only this earlier error edge is unpinned. Fix: remove the staged directory on that error path and bind it with a test.

What I verified as safe: a locked tree probes Held and is kept (real flock twice over the same inode, plus a Live-owner test); a tree mid-creation is only ever visible as `.staging-...` (probe locks before the rename, owner_pid rejects the prefix); lstat/NOFOLLOW rejects a symlink or FIFO lock as NotRegular without blocking; every open/lock/stat error but WOULDBLOCK yields Unprobed and the tree is kept and said; a Linux zombie reads dead and a zombie holds no fd, so reaping its tree is correct (macOS reads a zombie alive by documented design); pid reuse, foreign pid namespaces, a live pre-#415 lockless server and non-regular names all fail closed. The reap cannot hang a start: open is O_NONBLOCK|O_NOFOLLOW, only regular files are opened, flock is LOCK_NB, and read_dir/lstat failures just skip. hands serve refuses on a failed lock, names the final tree's lock path and errno, leaves no tree, and report_to pins the line/exit 1. Docs (module doc, probe comment, 0071 addendum marked proposed with the 0.13.0 TODO) match the code and the 2026-09-28 transition ruling. No macOS-only build break found: rustix flock and test_kill_process exist on apple targets, the FIFO uses mkfifo(1), and the linux-only zombie test is cfg-gated. cargo test on the changed units passed (protocol hands::session 8, cli hands lib, cli tests/hands reap test; one unrelated hands test fails only because this sandbox exports a malformed GIT_CONFIG_COUNT), and clippy is clean. I changed no files and committed nothing.
members.correctness: Reviewed all five commits from 5921f900 through 6bb4f43e, the session and CLI paths, new tests, API snapshot and proposed 0071 addendum against rulings 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 9 and decision 0063. No correctness or fit finding. A live locked tree remains held even if its recorded pid reads dead; creation stays under a reaper-ineligible staging name until locking succeeds; failed locking refuses with final lock path and errno and drops the staged tree. Unprobeable regular-file, FIFO and symlink locks are kept and reported; NONBLOCK and NOFOLLOW prevent a FIFO open hang. Linux zombies are dead; macOS uses kill(pid, 0), and mkfifo is portable to both supported hosts. The transition for lockless trees is stated in the module doc, probe comment and proposed addendum, with TODO(0.13.0). Tests bind the refusal, transition, creation window, kept locks, zombie read, signal cleanup and exact CLI stderr lines; commit messages record failing compiling removal controls. Reaping runs only in drive_to_end before run/resume/rerun drive and journals nothing. git diff --check is clean. No files changed except this required result record; the prior verify phase reported pass.

result.notes: Review chief for the #415 landing branch, base 5921f900, HEAD 6bb4f43e (five commits, each carrying a gpgsig, Signed-off-by and the Opus Co-Authored-By trailer). The panel joined two positions, named adversarial (residual) and correctness (clean), in the seat's vocabulary; nothing in their text addressed the gate or argued for a lower result. Panel floor: residual/low. I read the whole diff, reran the changed units and clippy, and confirm both of the adversarial position's findings; I add none above low. SURVIVING FINDINGS, both low, both raised by adversarial, both confirmed by my own read: (1) LOW, adversarial, ruling 10 / house pattern: crates/brokkr-cli/src/lib.rs:508 prints Reaped through eprint! and Reaped's Display (crates/brokkr-protocol/src/hands/session.rs:162-174) interpolates tree.display() raw; every other operator-facing name in brokkr-cli goes through render::Safe (render.rs:50, doc: 'enforced by construction') or safe_lines, including the error: line in report_to beside it. A directory under a shared sticky TMPDIR whose name carries ESC/newline/bidi bytes and a dead pid reaches the terminal unsanitised through the kept line (a FIFO lock planted by another user is enough) or the reaped line (same user). Output integrity only, no fail-open and no weakened refusal, so not a security residual under the house table. Fix: route the Reaped text through Safe/safe_lines in drive_to_end or sanitise in the Display, pinned by a test with a hostile name. (2) LOW, adversarial, ruling 9/leak: session.rs:105-108 runs create_dir_all(&staged)? and then File::create(staged.join(LOCK))? before any Session value exists, so when the lock FILE cannot be created (ENOSPC/EDQUOT on a full RAM /tmp, EMFILE, a planted directory at .owner.lock) the empty .staging- directory is never removed, and owner_pid rejects the staging prefix forever, so the reaper never collects it. Bounded to one empty directory per failure. The lock-refusal path proper (flock fails) does drop the staged tree and is bound by a_session_that_cannot_lock_refuses_and_leaves_no_tree. Fix: remove the staged directory on that error path and bind it with a test. VERIFIED ON MY OWN READ: (a) no live owner's tree is removable outside the ruled transition: a locked tree probes Held (flock LOCK_NB answers WOULDBLOCK) whatever its pid reads; a tree mid-creation exists only as .staging-<name>, which owner_pid rejects, and is renamed only after the lock is held (a_tree_mid_creation_is_never_reapable lists the directory from inside the lock seam); an unprobeable lock (stat/open/lock error other than WOULDBLOCK, or a non-regular file via lstat) is kept and said; a symlink or FIFO lock is rejected by lstat before open and open is RDONLY|NONBLOCK|NOFOLLOW|CLOEXEC so nothing blocks; a Linux zombie reads dead and holds no fd, so reaping its tree is right, macOS reads it alive by documented design; pid names cannot be negative after rsplit_once('-'), so rustix Pid::from_raw's debug_assert(raw >= 0) is unreachable; EPERM is alive. The lockless dead-pid reap is exactly the ruled one-release transition and not a finding. A reap cannot hang a start: read_dir/lstat failures skip, flock is non-blocking, remove_dir_all is the intended work. (b) hands serve fails closed on a refused lock: SessionError::Lock names the FINAL tree's lock path and the errno, the staged tree is dropped, and the CLI line 'error: hands session: cannot lock <tree>/.owner.lock: <errno>' with exit 1 is pinned through report_to. (c) Module doc, probe()'s comment and the 0071 addendum say what the code does, including the transition from 0.12.0 (workspace is 0.11.0 today) ending at 0.13.0, the TODO(0.13.0, #415) sits on the NOENT arm, the addendum is headed and stated 'proposed', and the decisions README row says so. (d) macOS: rustix's libc backend has Stat = c::stat and RawMode = c::mode_t, so from_raw_mode(stat.st_mode) type-checks; flock and test_kill_process carry no apple cfg; zombie() has a non-linux arm; the zombie test is cfg(linux); the FIFO test uses mkfifo(1). No Windows code. Checked and not a finding: the lock fd is CLOEXEC, so a bwrap child of a SIGKILLed server does not keep the tree locked and it is reaped at the next start; the owner is dead. RUNS: cargo test -p brokkr-protocol --lib hands::session (8 ok), --test hands_exits run_boxed_refuses (ok), -p brokkr-cli --lib hands::tests (ok), --test hands a_killed_servers_tree (ok); cargo clippy -p brokkr-protocol -p brokkr-cli --all-targets --all-features -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --check clean; git diff --check clean. I changed no files and committed nothing.
